chapter: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
title: Walter Fuller's small combo
summary: Five-piece band in cocktail lounges; long stays.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, did you stay with Fuller?
Yeah. We was out of a job for a while, then Fuller got this idea about the small combo.
Well, before we go into that, who was in the -- in Fuller's -- what'd you say, nine-piece band? Or eleven-piece band at the Grand Terrace?
Most of the Hines men. Omer Simeon who the stayed, I stayed/, Eck stayed on drums. I don't remember.
Was Oliver Coleman in the band then, or was that after Oliver?
I can't remember who the drummer was.
Well, who was in the small Fuller band?
Omer Simeon, Roselle Claxton on piano, Fuller on trumpet, and me on string bass.
Did you have drums?
Oh, yeah. Buddy Smith.
So it was a five-piece band?
Uh-huh.
Where'd you work?
Mostly cocktail lounges in and out of town. We worked the Capital, we worked in Peoria, Minneapolis, and you know, different cocktail lounges in and out of Chicago.
Fuller was a pretty good trumpet player.
Yes, he was.
Like Louie.
And singer, too.
And singer. Was he in -- it seems like I've seen where he's gotten credit -- partial credit for 'Rosetta.' Did he write the words?
He didn't write the words. He got credit for singing it. But I think Henry Woods wrote the music and the words, I think.
Were you glad to get off the
road? Or did you like traveling?
Well, I liked it when I went with Walter Fuller, because you stayed four weeks at the shortest.
Uh-huh. No one-nighters?

No one-nighters. Four weeks, with a two-week option, or four-week option. Sometimes you stayed eight weeks. Now, we was down in -- we stayed in Peoria, oh, about nine weeks. We stayed in Minneapolis at the Happy Hour about nine weeks, or more. No, we was there about -- well, it was nine weeks. ABout three or four months.
How long did that group stay together?
We stayed together, oh, almost two years.
